title: Set Operations, Power Sets, and Partitions
summary: This unit covers relations between sets (Teilmengenbeziehungen), central set operations (Mengenoperationen), and their connection to logical connectives (Junktoren). It also covers the universal set (Grundmenge), finite sets (endliche Mengen), cardinality (Mächtigkeit), power sets (Potenzmengen), families of sets (Mengenfamilien), partitions (Partitionen), membership patterns (Mitgliedschaftsmuster), Gray-code order (Gray-Reihenfolge), and Venn and Karnaugh–Veitch diagrams.
keyFacts: A nonempty universal set Ω is fixed for complements and Venn diagrams.
M₁⊆M₂ means that every element of M₁ is also in M₂; M₁⊂M₂ additionally requires M₁≠M₂.
M₁ and M₂ are disjoint if and only if M₁∩M₂=∅.
The union corresponds to inclusive OR, the intersection to AND, and the symmetric difference to exclusive OR.
Set difference is not symmetric: M₁∖M₂ and M₂∖M₁ may differ.
A finite set can be listed using finitely many elements; its cardinality counts distinct elements.
The power set 𝒫(M) contains exactly all subsets of M.
For a finite set M with k elements, |𝒫(M)|=2ᵏ.
The empty set is a subset of every set, but it is not automatically an element of every set.
The union of a family contains elements from at least one member of the family; the intersection contains only elements that belong to every member.
A partition consists of nonempty, pairwise disjoint blocks whose union is the entire universal set.
In a partition, each element belongs to exactly one block.
For n sets, there are 2ⁿ possible membership patterns.
In Gray-code order, adjacent cells differ in exactly one bit; some geometrically possible regions may be empty.

review.notes: Alle 44 Fragen geprüft. Mathematische Ausdrücke wurden konsequent in KaTeX gesetzt. Eine Teilmengenfrage und die Disjunktheitsfrage wurden gegen mehrdeutige Distraktoren abgesichert; die Boss-Frage zu Prädikaten wurde eindeutig formuliert. Keine Frage musste entfernt werden.

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes $M_1\subseteq M_2$?

options.text: Every element of $M_1$ is also in $M_2$.
There is an element in $M_1$ that is not in $M_2$.

questions.explanation: A subset contains only elements that also belong to the superset. A single element of $M_1$ outside $M_2$ would disprove the subset relation.

questions.prompt: Use the convention that $A\subset B$ means: $A\subseteq B$ and $A\ne B$. Assess the statement: If $A\subset B$, then $A$ and $B$ may be equal.
questions.explanation: Under the stated convention, the sets must be different when $A\subset B$.

questions.prompt: Select all correct statements. More than one answer may be correct.

options.text: $x\in M_1\cup M_2$ if and only if $x$ is in at least one of the two sets.
$x\in M_1\setminus M_2$ if and only if $x\in M_1$ and $x\notin M_2$.
$x\in\Omega\setminus M$ if and only if $x\in\Omega$ and $x\notin M$.
$x\in M_1\triangle M_2$ if and only if $x$ is in both sets.
$x\in M_1\cap M_2$ if and only if $x$ is in exactly one of the two sets.

questions.explanation: A union means membership in at least one set; a difference means membership in the first set but not the second; and a complement is formed within $\Omega$. “In both” describes the intersection, while “in exactly one” describes the symmetric difference.

questions.prompt: A fixed ___ is needed to take the complement of a set.
questions.explanation: A complement is defined relative to a specified universal set $\Omega$: $\Omega\setminus M$.

questions.prompt: Which condition characterizes exactly when two sets $M_1$ and $M_2$ are disjoint?
questions.explanation: Disjoint sets have no common elements. This is expressed precisely by $M_1\cap M_2=\varnothing$. The other conditions do not characterize disjointness in general.
The intersection contains exactly the elements that occur in both sets. Here, that is only $2$.

questions.prompt: Which condition is equivalent to $M_1=M_2$?
questions.explanation: Set equality is characterized by subset relations in both directions. A proper subset or a nonempty difference rules out equality.

questions.prompt: Select all correct correspondences. More than one answer may be correct.
questions.explanation: AND, OR, and NOT are represented by intersection, union, and complement. XOR corresponds to the symmetric difference, not the intersection.

questions.prompt: What is the cardinality of the set $\{a,a,b\}$?
questions.explanation: Repeated elements are not counted more than once in a set. The two distinct elements are $a$ and $b$.

questions.prompt: Which power set is correct?
questions.explanation: The empty set has exactly one subset, namely itself. Therefore, its power set contains the single element $\varnothing$.

questions.prompt: For $M=\{a,b,c\}$, which subset is represented by the bit string `101`?
questions.explanation: The first and third bits are $1$, so $a$ and $c$ belong to the subset. The middle bit is $0$, so $b$ does not belong to it.

questions.prompt: Suppose $M_1=\{0,1,2\}$ and $M_2=\{2,3\}$. Which set is $M_1\triangle M_2$?
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains elements that belong to exactly one set. These are $0$ and $1$ from $M_1$, and $3$ from $M_2$.

questions.prompt: Let $A=\{1,2,3\}$ and $B=\{2,3,4\}$. What is $A\setminus B$?
questions.explanation: $A\setminus B$ contains the elements of $A$ that are not in $B$. Only $1$ satisfies this condition.

questions.prompt: It follows from $M_1\cap M_2=\varnothing$ that $M_1$ and $M_2$ are disjoint.
questions.explanation: An empty intersection means that no element belongs to both sets. This is exactly the definition of disjointness.

questions.prompt: If $M$ has exactly four elements, then $|\mathcal P(M)|=___$.
questions.explanation: For a set with $k$ elements, the power set has $2^k$ elements. For $k=4$, this gives $2^4=16$.

questions.prompt: For $M=\{a,b,c\}$, which subset is represented by the bit string `010`?
questions.explanation: Only the second bit is $1$. Therefore, the subset contains only $b$.

questions.prompt: For $\mathcal S=\{\{1,2\},\{2,3\},\{2,4\}\}$: select all correct statements. More than one answer may be correct.

options.text: $3$ belongs to every member of $\mathcal S$.

questions.explanation: The union collects all elements that occur, while the intersection contains only those that the sets have in common. Thus $1$ belongs to the union and $2$ belongs to the intersection.

questions.prompt: Which family is a partition of $M=\{1,2,3,4\}$?
questions.explanation: The two blocks are nonempty, disjoint, and cover $M$ completely. The other options contain an overlap, an empty block, or omit an element.

questions.prompt: How many possible membership patterns are there for four sets?
questions.explanation: Each of the four sets contributes one yes/no bit. Thus, there are $2^4=16$ possible patterns.

questions.prompt: In Gray-code order, adjacent cells differ in exactly one bit.
questions.explanation: Gray-code order is arranged so that adjacent patterns differ in exactly one bit.

questions.prompt: Suppose $\Omega=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$ and $M_1=\{0,1,2\}$. What is $\Omega\setminus M_1$?
questions.explanation: The complement contains the elements of $\Omega$ that are not in $M_1$. These are $3$ and $4$.

questions.prompt: The statement $M_1\nsubseteq M_2$ is equivalent to $M_1\setminus M_2$ ___ $\varnothing$.
questions.explanation: A subset relation fails exactly when at least one element of $M_1$ lies outside $M_2$. Therefore, $M_1\setminus M_2$ is nonempty.

questions.prompt: For sets $A$ and $B$, $A\subseteq B$ means that every element of $A$ is also in $B$. The notation $A\subset B$ means that $A\subseteq B$ and $A\ne B$. Also, $X\setminus Y:=\{x\in X\mid x\notin Y\}$. Select all characterizations of $A\subset B$ that hold.
questions.explanation: A proper subset satisfies $A\subseteq B$ and differs from $B$. This is equivalent to at least one element of $B$ not belonging to $A$, that is, $B\setminus A\ne\varnothing$.

questions.prompt: Let $M_1=\{1,2\}$ and $M_2=\{2,3\}$. Which element is a counterexample to $M_1\subseteq M_2$?
questions.explanation: The element $1$ is in $M_1$ but not in $M_2$. A single such element is enough to disprove the subset relation.

questions.prompt: Set operations and logical connectives are not the same objects, but they have corresponding membership and truth conditions.
questions.explanation: A set and a truth value are different things. However, for the operations described, the conditions for membership and truth follow the same pattern.

questions.prompt: For an element $x\in\Omega$, the bit pattern `b1b2` encodes its membership: the first bit is `1` if and only if $x\in M_1$, and the second is `1` if and only if $x\in M_2$. A bit `0` means that $x$ is not in the corresponding set. Which patterns describe exactly the elements in $\Omega\setminus M_1$?
questions.explanation: The complement $\Omega\setminus M_1$ contains exactly the elements of $\Omega$ that are not in $M_1$. Therefore, the first bit must be `0`; the second bit can be either `0` or `1`. The matching patterns are `00` and `01`.

questions.prompt: When does an element $x$ belong to the union $\bigcup\mathcal S$ of a nonempty family of sets $\mathcal S$?

options.text: If $x$ belongs to at least one member of $\mathcal S$.
If $x$ is itself a member of $\mathcal S$.
If $x$ belongs to no member of $\mathcal S$.
If $x$ belongs to every member of $\mathcal S$.

questions.explanation: The union uses an existential condition: it is enough for $x$ to belong to at least one set in the family. “In every set” describes the intersection.

questions.prompt: Select all correct statements about finite sets and cardinality. More than one answer may be correct.

options.text: For some $k\in\mathbb N_0$, a finite set can be listed as $\{x_1,\ldots,x_k\}$.
Repeated elements in a listing do not increase the cardinality.
Cardinality counts every repetition as a new element.
All infinite sets have the same cardinality.

questions.explanation: Finiteness is defined by the existence of a finite listing, and cardinality counts only distinct elements. Infinite sets do not all automatically have the same cardinality.

questions.prompt: In a partition, every element of the universal set belongs to exactly one ___.
questions.explanation: The blocks of a partition cover the whole set and are pairwise disjoint. Therefore, each element belongs to exactly one block.

questions.prompt: Which family describes the partition of $\mathbb Z$ by remainders upon division by $3$?
questions.explanation: For $n=3$, there are three residue classes, $0$, $1$, and $2$ modulo $3$. They are nonempty, disjoint, and cover $\mathbb Z$.

questions.prompt: In a Venn diagram, all $2^n$ geometrically possible membership regions for $n$ sets must be nonempty.
questions.explanation: There are $2^n$ possible patterns, but some regions may be empty. The nonempty membership regions alone then form a partition of $\Omega$.

questions.prompt: How many possible membership patterns are there for five sets?
questions.explanation: Each of the five sets has two possible states. Therefore, there are $2^5=32$ possible bit patterns.

questions.prompt: Suppose $\Pi\subseteq\mathcal P(M)$, every block in $\Pi$ is nonempty, distinct blocks are disjoint, and $\bigcup\Pi=M$. Which conclusion is correct?

options.text: At least one element of $M$ belongs to no block.
Every element of $M$ belongs to at least two blocks.
All blocks must have the same cardinality.
Every element of $M$ belongs to at least one and at most one block.

questions.explanation: The union ensures complete coverage, and disjointness prevents an element from belonging to multiple blocks. Equal block sizes are not required for a partition.

questions.prompt: Let $A=\{0,1,2,4\}$ and $B=\{2,3,4\}$. Which set is $(A\setminus B)\cup(B\setminus A)$?
questions.explanation: $A\setminus B=\{0,1\}$ and $B\setminus A=\{3\}$. Their union contains exactly the elements that belong to one of the two sets, so it is the symmetric difference.

questions.prompt: Let $\Omega=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$. The solution sets of the predicates $P(x)$ and $Q(x)$ are $P=\{0,1,2\}$ and $Q=\{2,3\}$, respectively. Select all correct statements. More than one answer may be correct.

options.text: The solution set of $P(x)\land Q(x)$ is $\{2\}$.
The solution set of $P(x)\lor Q(x)$ is $\{0,1,2,3\}$.
The solution set of $\neg P(x)$ is $\{0,1,2,3\}$.

questions.explanation: OR, AND, and XOR correspond to union, intersection, and symmetric difference. The complement of $P$ in $\Omega$ would be $\{3,4\}$, and $P\setminus Q$ is $\{0,1\}$.

questions.prompt: Let $\Omega=\{1,2,3,4\}$, $A=\{1,2\}$, $B=\{1,2,3\}$, and $C=\{3,4\}$. Which statement is correct?
questions.explanation: $A$ contains exactly the elements $1$ and $2$, while $B$ also contains $3$. Thus $A$ is a proper subset of $B$, and $B\setminus A=\{3\}$; by contrast, $A$ and $C$ are disjoint.

questions.prompt: For a nonempty family of sets $\mathcal S$: $x\in\bigcap\mathcal S$ if and only if $x$ belongs to every member of $\mathcal S$.
questions.explanation: The intersection uses a universal condition. A single member of the family that does not contain $x$ is enough to show that $x$ is not in the intersection.

questions.prompt: In the partition $\{2\mathbb Z,1+2\mathbb Z\}$, $-3$ belongs to ___.
questions.explanation: $-3=1+2\cdot(-2)$, so $-3$ belongs to the odd residue class $1+2\mathbb Z$. Because the blocks are disjoint, it cannot also belong to the other block.

questions.prompt: For $\Omega=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, $M_1=\{0,1,2\}$, and $M_2=\{2,3\}$, what membership pattern does $x=4$ have?
questions.explanation: $4$ belongs to neither $M_1$ nor $M_2$, but it does belong to $\Omega$. Therefore, its pattern is `00`.

questions.prompt: Select all correct statements about the complement relative to the universal set used here. More than one answer may be correct.

options.text: The complement is always equal to $M$.
The complement is formed relative to a specified universal set $\Omega$.
$x\in\Omega\setminus M$ if and only if $x\in\Omega$ and $x\notin M$.

questions.explanation: The complement depends on $\Omega$ and contains elements of the universal set that are not in $M$. The expressions in c and d either reverse or ignore this condition.

questions.prompt: Which residue class modulo $3$ contains $-4$?
questions.explanation: $-4=2+3\cdot(-2)$. Therefore, $-4$ belongs to the residue class $2+3\mathbb Z$.

questions.prompt: For $A=\{x\in\Omega\mid P(x)\}$ and $B=\{x\in\Omega\mid Q(x)\}$, the condition $A\triangle B$ corresponds to the truth condition of which statement?
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains exactly the elements that belong to one set but not both. This corresponds to exclusive OR, or XOR.

questions.prompt: What relationship holds between the truth sets of $A$ and $B$ if $A\Rightarrow B$ is universally valid?

options.text: The two truth sets must be equal.
The truth set of $B$ is contained entirely in the truth set of $A$.
The truth set of $A$ is contained entirely in the truth set of $B$.
The two truth sets are disjoint.

questions.explanation: $A$ is a sufficient condition for $B$. Therefore, $A$ can be true only where $B$ is also true; in set-theoretic terms, the truth set of $A$ is a subset of the truth set of $B$.

questions.prompt: A claimed relation $M_1\subseteq M_2$ is to be disproved. Which observation is sufficient as a counterexample?

options.text: There is an $x$ such that $x\in M_2$ and $x\notin M_1$.
There is an $x$ such that $x\in M_1$ and $x\notin M_2$.
There is an $x$ such that $x\in M_1\cap M_2$.
$M_1$ and $M_2$ have at least one element in common.

questions.explanation: For the subset relation to hold, every element of $M_1$ must also belong to $M_2$. A single element of $M_1$ outside $M_2$ disproves this universal statement.

questions.prompt: You are filtering the cafeteria app. Which selection describes the intersection $V\cap H$ of vegetarian dishes and dishes available today?

options.text: Dishes that are vegetarian or available today.
Dishes that satisfy exactly one of the two properties.
Dishes that are vegetarian and available today.
Dishes that are vegetarian but not available today.

questions.explanation: The intersection corresponds to logical AND: both properties must hold at the same time.

questions.prompt: You are searching a university database for all materials on “networks” or “compilers.” Which set operation collects the results from both searches, including documents tagged with both keywords?
questions.explanation: The union corresponds to inclusive OR: results from both sets are included, including results that occur in both.

questions.prompt: You have a set with 8 distinct elements. How many subsets does its power set contain?
questions.explanation: For $k$ elements, $|\mathcal P(M)|=2^k$. So for 8 elements, the power set contains $2^8=256$ subsets.

questions.prompt: Your spam filter considers the universal set $\Omega$ of all emails received in one day; $S$ is the set marked as spam. Which statements are correct?

options.text: An email outside $\Omega$ still belongs to the complement relative to $\Omega$.
The result depends on the chosen universal set $\Omega$.

questions.explanation: A complement is always formed relative to the universal set. Thus, this refers exactly to the emails in $\Omega$ that are not in $S$.

questions.prompt: In a Git comparison, $A$ marks files changed in Branch A, and $B$ marks files changed in Branch B. You want to mark files changed in exactly one branch. Which operation should you use?
questions.explanation: The symmetric difference contains exactly the files that belong to one set but not both. This corresponds to XOR.

questions.prompt: You are testing a circuit with five yes/no inputs. How many rows does a complete truth table need so that each membership pattern appears once?
questions.explanation: Each of the 5 inputs has 2 states. Thus, there are $2^5=32$ possible patterns and, accordingly, 32 rows in the table.

questions.prompt: At a university tournament, all registered teams are assigned to nonempty groups. Which rule describes a partition of the set of teams?

options.text: Only teams with at least one win are assigned to a group.
Some groups are left empty as placeholders.
Each team is assigned to exactly one group; no group is empty, and the groups do not overlap.
A team may appear on several fan lists at the same time.

questions.explanation: A partition consists of nonempty, pairwise disjoint blocks whose union is the entire universal set.

questions.prompt: How many distinct nonnegative values can an unsigned 12-bit field store?
questions.explanation: Each bit can be 0 or 1. Therefore, there are $2^{12}=4096$ distinct bit strings and values from 0 to 4095.

questions.prompt: You are helping design a digital circuit. In which situation is Gray-code order useful in a Karnaugh–Veitch diagram?

options.text: All cells are sorted alphabetically by signal name.
Each cell is assigned a random bit string so that the measurement is unbiased.
Adjacent cells differ in exactly one input bit, making neighborhoods that can be simplified visible.
Adjacent cells must differ in every bit.

questions.explanation: In Gray-code order, adjacent cells differ in exactly one bit. This makes related cases visible for circuit simplification.

questions.prompt: A learning platform has four independent permissions: read, comment, export, and manage. What concept underlies a catalog that allows every possible combination of these permissions as a role?

options.text: The intersection, containing only permissions shared by all roles
The power set of the four permissions
A partition in which each permission appears in exactly one role
The complement, containing only permissions that have not been assigned

questions.explanation: Each role is a subset of the four permissions. The catalog of all possible roles is therefore the power set.
